sc: Child with VSD or RHD and dental caries, fever 2 weeks, splenomegaly, new murmur, haematuria → Infective endocarditis
Infant a week after a cold, tachycardia out of proportion to fever, gallop, no murmur → Coxsackie B myocarditis
Chest pain better on sitting forward, rub → Pericarditis
f: Prolonged fever, pallor, splenomegaly · new or changing murmur · splinter haemorrhages, Osler nodes (tender), Janeway lesions (painless) · haematuria
3 blood cultures from separate sites before antibiotics · echocardiography (vegetations) · ESR, CRP, urine
IV penicillin + gentamicin (strep) or cloxacillin (staph) for 4–6 weeks · prophylaxis: amoxicillin 50 mg/kg before dental work in high-risk
Myocarditis: heart failure without a murmur, soft sounds, high troponin · pericarditis: rub · tamponade: muffled sounds, pulsus paradoxus → pericardiocentesis
HCM: collapse during sport, family history of sudden death · dilated: post-myocarditis
trap: Secundum ASD almost never gets endocarditis · myocarditis has no significant murmur (a loud murmur = structural disease) · digoxin is used with great care in myocarditis
